question: Will the Panama Canal Authority reduce daily transit limits before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: 33 daily slots since Oct 15, 2026 (10 Neopanamax + 23 Panamax), up from 32 after better rain; Gatun ~85 ft in early Oct, above ACP projections and well above the ~79-80 ft that triggered the Nov 2023 cuts. Base rate: a Nov-Dec cut happened in recent years only in the 2023 strong El Nino year. Case for YES: a strong or record El Nino is forecast, ACP budgets 29.5 transits/day for FY2027, and ACP showed in Sept 2026 that it will cut early (~84 ft). If November rains fail, a cut effective in December is plausible. Case for NO: ACP is currently easing, its stated worry is the Jan-Apr dry season (a cut effective in January would not count), and only ~2.4 months remain. No matching human market: Polymarket only has 'US takes canal' (0.03) and 'effectively closed' contracts, which are different events and thinly traded.
calls.dossier:
- Status quo as of 2026-10-19: 33 daily slots (Neopanamax 10 = 9 booking + 1 auction; Panamax 23), effective Oct 15, 2026, per the ACP advisory of Sept 28, 2026 (newsroompanama, prensa.com, indexbox). Neopanamax draft 49 ft since Sept 28.
- 2026 timeline: 36 slots and 50 ft draft in early Aug (Gatun 87.7 ft in July). Aug 20 ACP announcement: 34 from Sept 3-4 (Neo 9, Panamax 25), then 32 from Sept 15 (Panamax 23) (newsroompanama Aug 23; DTN Sept 2). Infobae Oct 18 says draft went 50 to 48 ft; another source cites 47.5 ft from Oct 1, later overridden by 49 ft.
- Gatun Lake ~85.03 ft in early October 2026; described as not optimal for the season but above initial projections (metrolibre/tvn-2/prensa, late Sept to early Oct). For comparison, Gatun was ~79-80 ft in Oct-Nov 2023, when the cuts happened.
- ACP says the watershed deficit continues and the booking system is the only way to guarantee a transit (prensa.com, Oct 2026). Rainfall May-Aug 2026 was 34% below normal (Infobae, Oct 18).
- An FY2027 budget assumption of 29.5 daily transits was called a conservative planning scenario, not an operational plan; ACP said it would keep 32 'until further notice' (marineinsight, Sept 2026). ACP projects losing 743 ships in the FY starting Oct 1 (Infobae).
- NOAA (via Infobae, Oct 18, 2026): 75% chance of a record El Nino Oct-Dec 2026; 98% chance it persists into early 2027. Reported ACP concern focuses on the Jan-Apr 2027 dry season.
- Former administrator Quijano (Aug 2026): 'If the lakes aren't full by the end of November, we'll be in trouble in the summer.'
- 2023 analog: 32 slots from July 30, 2023; a record-dry October led to cuts to 31 (Nov 1), 25 (Nov 3), 24 (Nov 7), 22 (Nov 30), then 20 and 18 into early 2024.
- Base rates: over 2019-2025, a cut in daily slots took effect within Oct 20-Dec 31 only in 2023 (1 of ~7 years). Conditioned on strong El Nino years with restrictions already in place, 1 of 1 (2023), but in 2023 the lake was ~5 ft lower at this point.
- Resolution: resolves off an ACP announcement, made after question close and before Jan 1, 2027, of a reduction in the combined Neopanamax + Panamax daily slots taking effect before 2027. Draft-only changes do not count; a cut announced in December but effective in January does not count.
- Event window: question close (~Oct 19-20, 2026) to Dec 31, 2026; as of 2026-10-19 about 0% elapsed, ~73 days remain.
- Searched for but not found: any ACP advisory after Oct 15 signaling December slot changes; a current mid-October Gatun reading; a matching prediction market (Polymarket has only 'US takes canal' and 'effectively closed' contracts).
calls.reference_class: ACP daily-slot changes in the Oct 20-Dec 31 window, 2019-2025, plus El Nino years

calls.reasoning: Status quo: ACP raised capacity from 32 to 33 daily slots on Oct 15, 2026, citing improved rainfall and current/projected Gatun Lake (85.03 ft, well above Oct 2023's ~81 ft). A cut before 2027 needs an ACP reversal within ~10 weeks. Toward yes: a very strong El Niño (NOAA ~75% record-strength Oct-Dec), the ACP calling Sep-Nov rainfall decisive, the dry season starting mid-Dec, and 2023's analog with slot cuts in Nov and Dec. Toward no: the ACP just increased slots, the lake is healthier than in 2023, and the ACP tends to cut draft before slots. No matching human market found (Polymarket's US-takeover and 'effectively closed' markets are different contracts).
calls.dossier:
- Aug 20 2026 (ACP/safety4sea): ACP announced slot cuts: Neopanamax to 9 and Panamax to 25 from Sep 3 (36->34), Panamax to 23 from Sep 15 (total 32). Cause: May-Aug rainfall 34% below average, watershed inflows 44% below (TWS).
- Sep 11 2026 (Industrial Info): ACP said Sep-Nov rainfall 'will be decisive'; the dry season (Dec 2026-Apr 2027) is the key risk window; El Niño >90% chance of becoming very strong.
- Sep 28 2026 (ACP press release / Newsroom Panama / WorldCargo News): ACP announced an increase to 10 Neopanamax slots (9 booking + 1 auction) plus 23 Panamax = 33 daily, effective Oct 15 2026; Neopanamax draft raised to 49.0 ft. Gatun Lake was 85.03 ft at announcement. Basis: 'current and projected' lake level, near-average rainfall, water-saving measures.
- Oct 15 2026 (Infobae/EFE): 33 slots took effect; the ACP says a water deficit persists and booking is the only guarantee; no new cuts announced.
- Oct 6 2026 (gCaptain): ACP expands the Long-term Slot Allocation program (LoTSA) for Jan 3-Apr 3 2027 to Panamax locks, ~3 reserved slots/day each for Neopanamax and Panamax; no statement on total dry-season capacity.
- Vásquez (canal head) expects the El Niño to last ~8 months; ACP says it will make further adjustments if needed.
- Oct 18 2026 (Infobae): NOAA ~75% chance of record El Niño in Oct-Dec, 98% chance it persists into early 2027; the article cites 36->32 (stale vs the Oct 15 increase to 33).
- Analog 2023 (strong El Niño): lake ~81 ft in Oct 2023; ACP cut slots to 25 (early Nov) and 22 (Dec 1), then 24 in Feb 2024. Current lake is ~4 ft higher than at the same point in 2023.
- Status quo: 33 daily slots in force; no cut announced as of Oct 19 2026.
- Resolves off an ACP announcement of a reduction in combined Panamax+Neopanamax daily slot allocations that takes effect before 2027, not off draft changes or booking-rule tweaks.
- Event window: question close (~Oct 19 2026) -> Dec 31 2026; as of Oct 19, ~0% elapsed (about 10.5 weeks remain).
- Markets: no matching human market; Polymarket has 'US takes Panama Canal' and 'effectively closed' markets only (different contracts).
- Searched but not found: any ACP Gatun Lake projection for Dec 2026; any post-Oct 15 news of planned cuts; the readable text of advisory A-37-2026.
calls.reference_class: ACP slot-regime changes during El Niño years (2015-16, 2019-20, 2023-24); probability of a slot cut in a ~10-week Oct-Dec window given the lake is moderately below full

calls.reasoning: Status quo: the ACP just raised slots from 32 to 33 on Oct 15, 2026 because Gatun Lake recovered to about 85 ft. A Yes needs a new announced cut that takes effect by Dec 31, 2026, about 10 weeks away. In the 2023 El Niño the ACP cut slots in Nov-Dec, but from a much lower lake (~79-80 ft). The 2015-16 El Niño was handled mainly with draft limits. Pushing toward Yes: a strong El Niño, a possible dry-season start in late November, and a budget assuming 29.5 average transits for FY2027. Pushing toward No: ACP planning targets Jan-Apr/Feb-May, with long-term slot auctions starting Jan 3, so cuts are more likely timed for 2027. No matching human market found; the Polymarket 'US takes canal' and 'effectively closed' contracts are different events.

calls.dossier:
- Aug 24, 2026 (FreightWaves): ACP cut daily transits 36->34 effective Sep 4 and 34->32 effective Sep 15 (9 Neopanamax + 23 Panamax). May-Aug rainfall was 34% below average and watershed inflows 44% below average.
- TWS Maritime: the 32-slot regime took effect Sep 15; a planned Oct 1 draft cut to 47.5 ft was postponed; ACP 'may announce additional changes'.
- Sep 28, 2026 (Newsroom Panama/ACP): slots rose 32->33 effective Oct 15 (10th Neopanamax slot); draft raised to 49 ft; reasons were Gatun recovery, September rains and positive lake-level forecasts. Booking limits per customer were also relaxed.
- Mid-Oct 2026 (Spanish-language press): Gatun Lake at 85.03 ft, below optimal for the season but above projections. Normal is about 36 transits/day; Panamax is at 23 vs a normal 26.
- Oct 15, 2026 (ABC Color): ACP says the water deficit continues; it gave no specific dry-season prediction; about 51 vessels in queue.
- ACP FY2027 budget (Oct 1 start) assumes an average of 29.5 daily transits and a loss of about 743 ships, under a conservative severe-El-Niño scenario that the ACP says is not its current operating plan. A 44 ft Neopanamax draft scenario is included for Feb-May 2027.
- Advisory A-37-2026 (Oct 5): long-term slot packages cover Jan 3 - Apr 3, 2027; auctions Nov 17 (Neopanamax) and Nov 24 (Panamax pilot).
- Panama's meteorological institute: dry season may begin in the second half of November. NOAA: 63% odds of a very strong El Niño; about 98% odds El Niño persists into early 2027.
- Analog 2023: with Gatun ~79-80 ft, ACP cut 32->31 (early Nov), 25 (Nov), 24 (Dec), 22 (Feb), and reached 18 at the low point. Analog 2015-16: mainly draft restrictions.
- Status quo: 33 slots in effect since Oct 15; the latest move was an increase.
- Resolution: resolves off an ACP announcement (advisory or press release) reducing combined Panamax + Neopanamax daily slot allocations, announced after question close and taking effect before Jan 1, 2027. A cut taking effect in January 2027 does not count.
- Event window: question close (~Oct 19, 2026) -> Dec 31, 2026; as of 2026-10-19 about 0% of the window has elapsed (~73 days remain).
- Searched but not found: Oct/Nov rainfall data after mid-October; any ACP statement on slot levels for Nov-Dec; readable text of A-37 on slot counts; any matching human prediction market (only Polymarket 'US takes canal' and 'effectively closed' contracts, which are different events).
calls.reference_class: ACP slot-cut decisions in the Oct-Dec window during El Niño years (2015, 2023), conditional on lake level and recent direction of change

calls.reasoning: Status quo: 33 daily slots since Oct 15, 2026, after the ACP raised capacity citing a recovering Gatun Lake (~85 ft, 4-5 ft above the level at which the 2023 cuts happened). Base rate: a cut taking effect between late Oct and Dec 31 happened only in 2023 (1 of ~7 recent years), a strong El Nino year. Toward Yes: a record El Nino is forecast (dry Oct-Nov likely), the FY2027 budget assumes 29.5 transits a day, the ACP cuts early (it did at ~84 ft in Aug 2026), the dry season may start in late Nov, and reversing even one slot counts. Toward No: the ACP just eased, its stated focus is Jan-Apr 2027 and long-term slot packages start Jan 3, so a cut may be timed for January, which would not count; ~10 weeks remain.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agreed on the facts: 33 slots in force from Oct 15 (10 Neopanamax + 23 Panamax), Gatun Lake at ~85.03 ft in early October, the 2023 analog at ~79-81 ft, no ACP advisory after Oct 15, and no matching human market. Minor factual conflicts (stale Infobae figures of 32 slots and a 48 ft draft vs official 33 slots and 49 ft; NOAA odds reported as 75% record vs 63% very strong) do not change the direction and could not be settled further without web access. The real disagreement is judgment: whether the ACP times any cut for December (counts) or January (does not). I weigh the record El Nino, the ACP's willingness in Aug-Sep 2026 to cut early, and the low bar (dropping one slot counts) slightly more than the most cautious run did, against the fresh easing and the ACP's Jan-Apr framing. Landing ~0.27.
